correctness.rationale: For each odd prime p and s>=1, binomial coefficients of 2p^s make every noncritical input mod p a normalized p-adic isometry. Reflective pairs have exactly the same image ball and distinct pairs have disjoint mod-p outputs. The critical center -1/2 has an exact quadratic unit-scaled square form after an integral isometric coordinate change. Thus all fibers follow from square-root counts, including small k and k=s+2 boundary. Counts of square units in even valuation layers give the exact finite image and Haar density. The checker exhaustively verified every output fiber in thirty finite parameter/depth cases; symbolic proof establishes all levels.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons distinguish two independent-input even-power sums (Arias–Borja–Anaya 2023), and finite-field results for different polynomial value questions (Ding–Zieve 2023), from the exact one-variable consecutive-input prime-power fiber theorem. Closest published records concern 2-adic unrestricted sums, three-adic modular Waring lengths, or a different polynomial. Current ledger statement searches locate previous consecutive-power results at p=2 or different exponents, not this theorem. General p-adic Morse methods might implicitly imply the local structure, and unindexed equivalent formulas are a real remaining risk.
residual_risks: A general p-adic Morse lemma or isometric change-of-variable theorem could make aspects of this specific branch decomposition implicit in older literature, but no equivalent all-prime exact fiber formula has been located.
Published research-record matches other than primary papers were compared only at indexed-summary level, not by reading all full manuscripts.
Failure of a search to locate an exact match is not evidence of mathematical uniqueness.

value.rationale: Consecutive-input sums of two large even powers are a natural restrictive variant of modular Waring and binary power-sum solvability. The uniform theorem determines both local solvability and exact target multiplicities across every odd prime and all exponents of the form 2p^s, with an exceptional scaled-square branch and a surprisingly small explicit density. This is a structural family-wide classification, not a routine evaluation of a known unrestricted power-sum image.
